diagram_math_checks.objects: Two vertices s,g; admissible actions A(s)={a,b}, A(g)={d}.
diagram_math_checks.check: These are exactly the state/action domain in the Example and the finite-model interface in def-learned-mdp-model. No extra vertex or action is drawn.
The Example says action a at s moves to g with reward 1; both models agree on (s,a). The sole intervertex directed arrow has precisely this source, target and reward.
The right self-loop encodes the Example dummy action d at g with reward 0 in both models.

The left self-loop encodes the shared self-transition for b, true reward 0 and learned reward 1. The hat is the existing label convention explained in the immediately preceding prose; it does not introduce a new admissible action.

Under the specified policy, s occurs only at time 0, a reaches g deterministically, and d remains at g. Therefore the reachable pair union is B for H>=2, with reward sequence 1,0,... in both models. This agrees with Verification steps 1.1 and 2.1 and the zero-error case of thm-single-policy-finite-horizon-simulation-bound. No diagram claim implies accuracy on (s,b).
Standalone final original-resolution PNG shows exactly two vertices, one s-to-g arrow and the two self-loops, all three labels visible without overlap. No closure/commutativity claim is present.
